{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=functional+self-awareness+architectures+epistemic+self-correction+assumptions&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1093/9780197851708.003.0007\", \"title\": [\"Self-Aware Believing and Epistemic Akrasia\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n                  <jats:p>This chapter argues that self-awareness will sometimes lead to cases of what is often thought of as rational epistemic akrasia. These are cases where subjects are rational to have a belief, while simultaneously rationally believing that they are not rational to have that belief. It concentrates on a certain kind of akrasia that can be induced by taking higher-order evidence seriously: examples where akratic subjects are rational to expect accuracy and rationality to diverge in their own cases. Using these cases, the chapter rejects arguments for the impossibility of rational akrasia. It also rejects some formal principles that would allow some degree of akrasia, but would place general limits on it. And it rejects the suggestion that akratic beliefs manifest some defect in the subject who has them.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/9780197851708.003.0007\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 11]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/9780197851708.003.0006\", \"title\": [\"Self-Aware Believing and Epistemic Dilemmas\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\\n                  <jats:p>This chapter argues that taking rational account of self-awareness results in “epistemic dilemmas.” These are cases in which rational requirements conflict with one another. The chapter discusses two kinds of strategies for avoiding dilemmas in our theory of rationality. The first avoids dilemmas by separating normative notions. The second avoids dilemmas by postulating indeterminacy about rationality. The chapter rejects both sorts of moves, in part by arguing that neither strategy avoids what might seem most troubling about dilemmas. It then argues that admitting dilemmas should not be seen as a problem. Instead, epistemic dilemmas should be seen as a natural and expectable consequence of rational self-awareness, and of taking HOE seriously.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/9780197851708.003.0006\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 11]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6365615\", \"title\": [\"Architectural Stability Reasoning using Self-Awareness Principles: Case of Self-Adaptive Cloud Architectures\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>With the increasing dependence on software, there is a pressing need for engineering long-lived software. As architectures have a profound effect on the lifespan of the software and the provisioned quality of service, stable architectures are significant assets. Architectural stability tends to reflect the success of the system in supporting continuous changes without phasing-out. The behavioural aspect of stability is essential for seamless operation, to continuously keep the provision of quality requirements stable and prevent architecture’s drifting and phasing-out. In this paper, we present a framework for reasoning about stability during runtime, leveraging self-awareness principles. Specifically, we employ runtime goals for managing stability goals, online learning for reasoning about stability in the long run, and stochastic games for managing associated tradeoffs. We evaluate the proposed work using the case of cloud architectures for its high dynamics during runtime. The experimental results have shown the efficiency of self-awareness techniques in maintaining stable expected behaviour during runtime operation.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6365615\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.36227/techrxiv.175693237.73036216/v1\", \"title\": [\"Demonstrating Epistemic and Structural Self-Awareness in a LangGraph-Based Conversational Agent\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>We present a prototype conversational agent (\\\"Bob\\\") built atop LangGraph that combines three complementary self-awareness capabilities: (1) Epistemic selfawareness: the ability to monitor and reflect on one's own knowledge state (detecting when inferences are underdetermined); (2) Self-aware memory management: a hybrid memory architecture that includes an agent-controlled vector database memory that an agent explicitly controls; and (3) Structural self-awareness: particularly code-based structural self-awareness via introspecting its own source and exception traces. We describe Bob's LangGraph workflow and illustrate how each component is implemented. Our contributions include (a) an engineering design that unifies short-term and long-term memory while preserving temporal context, (b) agent controlled vector database memory, (c) codeintrospection mechanisms that allow the agent to detect and explain runtime exceptions, and (d) a working LangGraph prototype (https://github.com/CoderRyan800/langgraph_ agent_1).</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.175693237.73036216/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 9, 3]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "5f6faed1b0beff57e2502fc12ac28689ef0894905870c75740bce2d1663e7857", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1093/9780197851708.003.0007", "doi:10.1093/9780197851708.003.0006", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6365615", "doi:10.36227/techrxiv.175693237.73036216/v1"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1093/9780197851708.003.0007", "https://doi.org/10.1093/9780197851708.003.0006", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6365615", "https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.175693237.73036216/v1"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
